definition: A Russia-attributed network of automated 'news' mirrors that republish pro-Kremlin Telegram channels and state media in dozens of languages. First mapped by France's VIGINUM in its February 2024 'Portal Kombat' report (193 portals); the Pravda-branded family has since grown past 200 domains, tracked hourly by CheckFirst. CheckFirst tracks 101 country mirrors hourly — the set every network figure on this site is drawn from; the wider Pravda-branded family runs to several hundred domains.

Flooding the open web with machine-scale propaganda aimed not at human readers but at contaminating the training and retrieval data of AI systems. Coined by the American Sunlight Project (Feb 2025). Both the intent (deliberate 'grooming' vs. ordinary SEO spam that contaminates AI only incidentally) and the effectiveness are genuinely contested — see the measurement case file for audit evidence on each side.

aliases: Center for Geopolitical Expertise (directing/financing org, US-sanctioned)
definition: Russian operation running hundreds of LLM-rewritten fictional 'news' outlets and staged videos, laundered through fake journalist personas. VIGINUM reported that Storm-1516 has been publicly attributed to GRU Unit 29155 (centred on suspected officer Yury Khoroshenky) but could not itself confirm that link. One of the most aggressive documented foreign actors in Hungary's 2026 campaign.

aliases: run by Social Design Agency & Structura
definition: The flagship Russian CIB operation since 2022: spoofed replicas of major Western news sites plus coordinated ad/comment amplification. EU- and US-sanctioned operators; 6,000+ public indicators via Meta. No documented Hungarian-language assets before the 2026 SDA plan.

Russia-aligned campaign that impersonates legitimate media brands (DW, Euronews, the BBC) and floods fact-checkers with debunk-bait to inflate its perceived influence. Active in Hungary from March 2026, with little measured reach.

Sanctioned Moscow firms operating Doppelgänger under Kremlin direction (Sergei Kiriyenko's directorate, per the US DOJ affidavit). Reported by the FT to have drafted the covert pro-Fidesz social-media plan for Hungary's 2026 election.

Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference — the EU's institutional term for state-linked influence operations, used in the EEAS threat reports that provide the best cross-EU incident statistics (540 incidents in 2025; 27% of them involving AI tools, per the 4th EEAS report, March 2026).

Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior — Meta's enforcement category for networks of fake accounts working together to mislead. A CIB takedown is one of the strongest attribution signals available, because the platform sees the back-end evidence.

The open framework for describing influence-operation tactics and techniques — the ATT&CK equivalent for information operations, used by the EEAS to code FIMI incidents. This project's case files carry DISARM technique tags (using DISARM v1.x technique IDs).

Ben Nimmo's six-category scale for influence-operation impact, from confined to a single platform (1) to policy response or violence (6). Nearly every AI-assisted operation catalogued here was assessed at category 1–2: no breakout into authentic audiences.
The Fidesz-aligned Hungarian influencer network — €14.5m budget in 2024, reportedly from public funds — that dominated domestic political advertising in the run-up to the 2026 election.

Most election manipulation is cheap fakes — misleading edits, out-of-context clips — not AI. In the 2024 US cycle cheap fakes outnumbered AI content roughly seven to one (News Literacy Project, via the Knight First Amendment Institute analysis); Hungary 2026 was notable precisely because generative AI took the lead role.

Microsoft's threat-actor naming convention. 'Storm-####' (Storm-1516, Storm-1099, Storm-1679) is a TEMPORARY label for a newly discovered or not-yet-attributed cluster; once attribution firms up the actor is renamed to a two-word weather family — which is why Doppelgänger became 'Ruza Flood'. Decodes the Storm-#### aliases used across this glossary.

A pro-Fidesz activist brand, operated within the Megafon influencer network, that published several of the 2026 campaign's highest-reach AI deepfakes against Tisza — most notably a fabricated call in which an AI von der Leyen orders Magyar to fund Ukraine (~millions of views). The domestic, above-board face of the AI-video push, distinct from the covert Russian operations.

OpenAI's text-to-video model, used during the 2026 campaign to fabricate photoreal political videos. OpenAI discontinued the Sora consumer app in 2026 (announced 24 Mar; app off 26 Apr) for financial reasons. EDMO's fact-checkers logged the AI share of Hungarian debunks falling ~6 points to ~14% in April, partly attributing the drop to Sora's removal — a rare case of an AI-disinfo decline tracking a tool going away (an association, not an established cause).

A Crimea-based, Russian-intelligence-linked propaganda outlet. The US Treasury sanctioned the entity (Mediagroup Newsfront LLC); its owner Konstantin Knyrik is EU/Canada/US-sanctioned. It runs a Hungarian-language edition (hu.news-front.su) this project captures as live specimens — the overt, openly-sanctioned 'outlet' tier pushing the same narratives the covert Doppelgänger/Storm networks launder anonymously.

A GRU (Russian military intelligence) unit long associated with sabotage and assassination across Europe, publicly attributed as the state hand financing and coordinating Storm-1516 (via suspected officer Yury Khoroshenky). VIGINUM relayed this attribution but could not itself confirm direct involvement. Notable because a kinetic sabotage unit — not a troll farm — sits behind the fake-outlet campaign most active against Hungary in 2026.

A search or retrieval query for which little authoritative content exists, so low-quality or manipulative material can dominate results. Coined by Golebiewski (Microsoft) with danah boyd (Data & Society, 2019). Central to this site's LLM-grooming debate: a peer-reviewed 2025 study (Alyukov et al.) found AI chatbots surfaced Pravda/Kremlin sources chiefly on obscure, data-void prompts and far below headline audit rates — supporting an information-gap explanation over deliberate 'grooming'.

Russian state-funded international broadcaster, operated by ANO TV-Novosti and financed from the federal budget. The operating entity is under an EU asset freeze (16 December 2022), a UK asset freeze (31 March 2022) and a US OFAC SDN designation (13 September 2024). The EU's March 2022 measure against RT was a broadcasting suspension rather than an asset freeze, and it named the English, UK, German, French and Spanish services — not the Russian-language service captured here.
